title: Polyphenol-rich extract from Torreya grandis peel attenuates lipopolysaccharide-induced inflammation in RAW264.7 macrophages via inhibition of the TLR4/NF-kappaB pathway.
authors: Zongo, Abel Wend-Soo; Gao, Kaili; Zaongo, Silvere D; Zogona, Daniel; Xu, Duoxia; Yu, Ningxiang; Meng, Xianghe
one_liner_zh: 研究香榧果皮多酚提取物通过TLR4/NF-kB通路抗炎，分子对接仅涉及蛋白-小分子，非蛋白质-DNA互作，无AI或物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: Torreya grandis (TG) peel is an overlooked byproduct, often discarded as waste during the processing of TG nuts, despite its potential as a good source of health-promoting bioactive compounds. To explore the potential of TG peel as a value-added resource, this study examined the phenolic composition and anti-inflammatory activity of its polyphenol extract (TGAP) using a lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-stimulated RAW264.7 macrophage model. The results show that flavonoids were the dominant phenolic class in TGAP, with major compounds including hesperidin O-glucuronic acid, naringenin 7-O-neohesperidoside, chrysoeriol 7-O-hexoside, daidzein, orobol, and epigallocatechin. TGAP treatment (50-200 mug mL(-1)) significantly reduced intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels by 8-68% and mitigated LPS-induced inflammation by decreasing nitric oxide production and downregulating pro-inflammatory mediators, including iNOS, COX-2, interleukin-1beta (IL-1beta), IL-2, IL-6, and TNF-alpha, at both the mRNA and protein levels. It was found that TGAP decreased Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4) expression and inhibited NF-kappaB signaling by preventing IkappaBalpha phosphorylation and nuclear translocation of the NF-kappaB p65 subunit, suggesting that TGAP exerts its anti-inflammatory effects through the inhibition of the TLR4/NF-kappaB pathway. Molecular docking also revealed that key TGAP polyphenols, including epigallocatechin, chrysoeriol, daidzein, genistein, hesperidin, and naringenin, exhibited strong binding affinities (-7.0 to -8.3 kcal mol(-1)) with TLR4 and NF-kappaBp65 proteins, primarily through hydrogen bonding, pi-stacking interactions, and van der Waals forces. These results suggest that these compounds play a central role in the anti-inflammatory activity of TGAP. Overall, TGAP is a promising natural anti-inflammatory agent, with potential therapeutic applications in inflammatory disorders.
abstract_zh: 香榧（Torreya grandis, TG）果皮是一种被忽视的副产物，在TG坚果加工过程中常作为废弃物丢弃，尽管其具有作为促进健康生物活性化合物良好来源的潜力。为探索TG果皮作为增值资源的潜力，本研究采用脂多糖（LPS）刺激的RAW264.7巨噬细胞模型，考察了其多酚提取物（TGAP）的酚类组成及抗炎活性。结果表明，黄酮类化合物是TGAP中主要的酚类类别，主要化合物包括橙皮苷O-葡萄糖醛酸、柚皮素7-O-新橙皮糖苷、金圣草素7-O-己糖苷、大豆苷元、奥罗波尔和表没食子儿茶素。TGAP处理（50-200 μg mL⁻¹）显著降低了细胞内活性氧（ROS）水平8-68%，并通过减少一氧化氮产生和下调促炎介质（包括iNOS、COX-2、白细胞介素-1β（IL-1β）、IL-2、IL-6和TNF-α）在mRNA和蛋白水平上缓解了LPS诱导的炎症。研究发现，TGAP通过阻止IκBα磷酸化和NF-κB p65亚基的核转位，降低了Toll样受体4（TLR4）表达并抑制NF-κB信号通路，表明TGAP通过抑制TLR4/NF-κB通路发挥其抗炎作用。分子对接还揭示，TGAP中的关键多酚，包括表没食子儿茶素、金圣草素、大豆苷元、染料木素、橙皮苷和柚皮素，与TLR4和NF-κBp65蛋白表现出强结合亲和力（-7.0至-8.3 kcal mol⁻¹），主要通过氢键、π-堆积相互作用和范德华力实现。这些结果表明，这些化合物在TGAP的抗炎活性中发挥核心作用。总体而言，TGAP是一种有前景的天然抗炎剂，在炎症性疾病中具有潜在的治疗应用价值。
